newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call rates up ahead of festive season.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call rates up ahead of festive season.

text.p: Dutch call money peaked at a month-high on Friday as market players scrambled to cover themselves ahead of the weekend and festive bank holidays.

"Banks want money to keep them from going into deficit and drawing on their secured loans quota with the Central Bank over the weekend. Given they will again need money midway through next week, ahead of yet another weekend, the price of call rose quite substantially today," one dealer said.
Call money was first quoted at 2.88 percent bid, later rising to 3.0 with most deals done at 3.06 pct, traders said.
Call was little offered, with one trader speculating sellers might step into the market later in the afternoon after having established the day's payments flows.
"Call may return to slightly lower levels later in the day and will probably be further down on Monday," he said.
On Thursday, overnight money was quoted at around 2.81/94 bid/offer. All other Dutch money market rates were unchanged in quiet trade.
One dealer said call money was set to rise again next Friday, but was unlikely to reach today's levels.
"Banks will better know their position as regards the secured loans quota which is due to expire (in mid-January). They might be less hesitant use it," he said.
The guilder traded at 112.250/650 per 100 marks.
